## Cleaning
Clean your jewellery with a small amount of mild soap in lukewarm water and a soft toothbrush, focusing on hard-to-reach areas. Rinse if needed and dry with a soft, lint-free cloth. Never use soap or a toothbrush on MARINE pearls: wipe them with a soft, slightly damp cloth instead.

Don't scrub hard: even PVD gold-plated stainless steel can dull over time. Avoid chemical cleaners and alcohol wipes.

Buff with a microfibre or jewellery polishing cloth to brighten the surface. This won't remove scratches or dents.

## Storage
Store your pieces somewhere dry and cool, away from direct sunlight. Keep them off wood and out of bathrooms or damp areas.

## When to take it off
We recommend taking your jewellery off before showering. Remove it before sweating, swimming, or applying skincare, perfume or hair products. Jewellery isn't made to be worn 24/7, so rotate your pieces.

## Pearls and stones
Natural stones and pearls need extra care. See the Pearl Care guide for MARINE pieces.

## Our base metal
Every Parure piece starts with 316L stainless steel, often called surgical-grade steel. It's strong, doesn't rust, and contains over 60% recycled content.

## Gold pieces (SOLAR and MARINE)
Our gold pieces are coated using PVD (physical vapour deposition), which bonds a thin layer of gold-tone coating to the steel. PVD is much harder-wearing than traditional electroplating, so the colour lasts longer and is resistant to tarnishing.

## Silver-tone pieces (LUNAR)
LUNAR pieces are not plated. They're polished 316L stainless steel in its natural silver tone. Because there's no coating, the colour can't wear off. They are not sterling silver.

## Stones and pearls
- **SOLAR:** red agate, a natural stone.
- **MARINE:** freshwater pearls and blue enamel.
- **LUNAR:** star-cut cubic zirconia crystals.

## Sensitive skin
316L stainless steel is hypoallergenic and meets the EU Nickel Directive limits for jewellery, so most people with sensitive skin can wear our pieces without irritation. If you have a severe, diagnosed nickel allergy, please email hello@parurelondon.com before ordering and we'll talk you through it.

The freshwater pearls in our MARINE collection are natural and softer than our steel. They need more care than the rest of our jewellery.

## Water
Keep pearls out of water. Don't swim, shower or bathe in MARINE pieces. If they get wet, pat them dry straight away with a soft cloth and let them air dry flat.

Put your MARINE pieces on after perfume, hairspray and make-up, and take them off before anything else. Chemicals and oils can dull the pearl's surface.

Wipe pearls gently with a soft, dry or slightly damp cloth after wearing. Never use soap, jewellery cleaner or a toothbrush on pearls.

## Storage
Store MARINE pieces flat in their pouch, separately from other jewellery, so harder metals and crystals can't scratch the pearls.

cited.title: Jewellery Care > Jewellery Care
cited.text:
## Cleaning
Clean your jewellery with a small amount of mild soap in lukewarm water and a soft toothbrush, focusing on hard-to-reach areas. Rinse if needed and dry with a soft, lint-free cloth. Never use soap or a toothbrush on MARINE pearls: wipe them with a soft, slightly damp cloth instead.

Don't scrub hard: even PVD gold-plated stainless steel can dull over time. Avoid chemical cleaners and alcohol wipes.

Buff with a microfibre or jewellery polishing cloth to brighten the surface. This won't remove scratches or dents.

## Storage
Store your pieces somewhere dry and cool, away from direct sunlight. Keep them off wood and out of bathrooms or damp areas.

## When to take it off
We recommend taking your jewellery off before showering. Remove it before sweating, swimming, or applying skincare, perfume or hair products. Jewellery isn't made to be worn 24/7, so rotate your pieces.

## Pearls and stones
Natural stones and pearls need extra care. See the Pearl Care guide for MARINE pieces.

cited.title: Pearl Care (MARINE) > Pearl Care (MARINE)
cited.text:
The freshwater pearls in our MARINE collection are natural and softer than our steel. They need more care than the rest of our jewellery.

## Water
Keep pearls out of water. Don't swim, shower or bathe in MARINE pieces. If they get wet, pat them dry straight away with a soft cloth and let them air dry flat.

## Last on, first off
Put your MARINE pieces on after perfume, hairspray and make-up, and take them off before anything else. Chemicals and oils can dull the pearl's surface.

## Cleaning
Wipe pearls gently with a soft, dry or slightly damp cloth after wearing. Never use soap, jewellery cleaner or a toothbrush on pearls.

## Storage
Store MARINE pieces flat in their pouch, separately from other jewellery, so harder metals and crystals can't scratch the pearls.

cited.title: Materials and Skin Sensitivity > Materials and Skin Sensitivity
cited.text:
## Our base metal
Every Parure piece starts with 316L stainless steel, often called surgical-grade steel. It's strong, doesn't rust, and contains over 60% recycled content.

## Gold pieces (SOLAR and MARINE)
Our gold pieces are coated using PVD (physical vapour deposition), which bonds a thin layer of gold-tone coating to the steel. PVD is much harder-wearing than traditional electroplating, so the colour lasts longer and is resistant to tarnishing.

## Silver-tone pieces (LUNAR)
LUNAR pieces are not plated. They're polished 316L stainless steel in its natural silver tone. Because there's no coating, the colour can't wear off. They are not sterling silver.

## Stones and pearls
- **SOLAR:** red agate, a natural stone.
- **MARINE:** freshwater pearls and blue enamel.
- **LUNAR:** star-cut cubic zirconia crystals.

## Sensitive skin
316L stainless steel is hypoallergenic and meets the EU Nickel Directive limits for jewellery, so most people with sensitive skin can wear our pieces without irritation. If you have a severe, diagnosed nickel allergy, please email hello@parurelondon.com before ordering and we'll talk you through it.

cited.title: Jewellery Care > Jewellery Care
cited.text:
## Cleaning
Clean your jewellery with a small amount of mild soap in lukewarm water and a soft toothbrush, focusing on hard-to-reach areas. Rinse if needed and dry with a soft, lint-free cloth. Never use soap or a toothbrush on MARINE pearls: wipe them with a soft, slightly damp cloth instead.

Don't scrub hard: even PVD gold-plated stainless steel can dull over time. Avoid chemical cleaners and alcohol wipes.

Buff with a microfibre or jewellery polishing cloth to brighten the surface. This won't remove scratches or dents.

## Storage
Store your pieces somewhere dry and cool, away from direct sunlight. Keep them off wood and out of bathrooms or damp areas.

## When to take it off
We recommend taking your jewellery off before showering. Remove it before sweating, swimming, or applying skincare, perfume or hair products. Jewellery isn't made to be worn 24/7, so rotate your pieces.

## Pearls and stones
Natural stones and pearls need extra care. See the Pearl Care guide for MARINE pieces.
